transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-18
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samantha Ortiz (HelioScale - Head of Partnerships), Liam Park (HelioScale - Enterprise AE), Rina Patel (HelioScale - Security Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Discussed joint GTM approach, who owns which accounts, pilot scope; decided to have Redwood provide tech appendix and HelioScale to supply security questionnaire.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay hey everyone thanks for joining, we're super excited to strategize the co-sell plan with HelioScale. Quick around-the-room?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Samantha): hi, Samantha here. we'll focus on mid-market accounts first, about 8-10 priority logos. looking forward to mapping.
00:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): Diego from Redwood, i'll handle the technical appendices, perf notes and pilot design.
00:45 Speaker 4 (Liam): Liam, i'll be working the accounts with Samantha, should be good.
:58 Speaker 2 (Samantha): quick note, we have a handful of customers that require VPC or strict data residency so we need clarity on private deployments and KMS integration.
01:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): absolutely. Redwood Private and Dedicated are the levers, and we have KMS integrations. we'll get Rina the compliance contacts and docs.
02:00 Speaker 3 (Diego): for pilot perf baseline, curious about typical sequence lengths and concurrency — that drives whether we recommend quantized variants or standard fp16. any idea from HelioScale?
02:22 Speaker 4 (Liam): most of the initial flows are short prompts, <256 tokens, but some agents chain prompts so we might have occasional long tails.
02:41 Speaker 3 (Diego): ok that suggests we optimize for low-latency tails and enable KV caching. we'll note that in the appendix.
03:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): for GTM economics, we propose revenue share on net-new deals and co-sell credits for demos. we should align on discount bands for committed pilots.
03:36 Speaker 2 (Samantha): can you sketch a simple grid? we need to know threshold for reserved capacity vs hosted consumption; some of our accounts won't accept hosted.
04:01 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we'll include a matrix: hosted per-token pricing, dedicated reserved monthly tiers, and private deployment license + support.
04:28 Speaker 4 (Liam): competitor question — we've had customers ask about AWS Marketplace procurement for in-cloud procurement. how does Redwood show up in that picture?
04:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): we integrate with marketplace workflows in a few clouds, but procurement preferences differ. mention to customers, won't block us but we'll include procurement options in the deck.
05:15 Speaker 5 (Rina): security gating — SOC2 is fine, but we need ok on data retention and ability to use our KMS. also audit logs for model queries.
05:36 Speaker 3 (Diego): we support customer-managed KMS and have per-request audit logs with trace IDs. we'll attach an example schema.
06:00 Speaker 5 (Rina): perfect, also share any pen-test results or third-party audits.
06:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll share SOC2 and an overview of pen testing; Diego will include the technical controls in appendix.
06:48 Speaker 2 (Samantha): back to pipeline — here's our preliminary top-10 accounts: Northbridge, Solaire Health, MeridianPay, NovaRetail, AegisTech, (names anonymized in chat). We should assign who leads outreach.
07:10 Speaker 4 (Liam): i can own Northbridge and NovaRetail with Samantha supporting the exec intro.
07:26 Speaker 2 (Samantha): yay we'll coordinate.
07:34 Speaker 3 (Diego): technical ask — for Northbridge, they want a 2-week perf run. We can do a scoped pilot on dedicated instances; need to confirm expected qps and dataset size.
07:58 Speaker 4 (Liam): estimated qps is 40 steady with peaks to 120 for batch windows, dataset is ~200k rows for embeddings.
08:18 Speaker 3 (Diego): that'll map to a small dedicated pool; i'll draft recommended instance sizing and a sample SLO.
08:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): timeline wise, propose: share deck + pricing (by 10/20), security docs (10/21), perf appendix (10/22), then exec intro week of 10/26, pilot kickoff first week of November. thoughts?
09:05 Speaker 2 (Samantha): timeline looks fine, just need alignment on pricing bands for pilots so we can commit to buyers.
09:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll put a couple of pilot templates — 2-week evaluation, 6-week POC with reserved capacity options.
09:40 Speaker 5 (Rina): also confirm we can do VPC peering for the pilot; some of our security teams insist on it.
10:01 Speaker 3 (Diego): VPC peering and private deployment options available but depends on region and infra. i'll scope the minimal network steps and what we need from HelioScale infra team.
10:28 Speaker 2 (Samantha): good. also, for our sales ops, we need a one-pager that explains co-sell motion and who owns renewal. we don't want to confuse customers.
10:46 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll include ownership rules: HelioScale leads ACV & renewal, Redwood owns infra and tiering for technical support during pilot, joint executive sponsorship for strategic deals.
11:15 Speaker 4 (Liam): question on credits — can Redwood provide demo credits that HelioScale can hand to prospects?
11:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we can provide limited demo credits for accredited partners; we'll include process in the deck.
11:48 Speaker 5 (Rina): will need to know data handling for demo creds — are logs kept? where do they land?
12:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): logs for demo are retained per tenant policy, and can be disabled or forwarded to customer syslog; we'll document.
12:30 Speaker 2 (Samantha): ok moving to objections — cost vs latency. some customers ask if cheaper quantized models are substantially worse for quality.
12:50 Speaker 3 (Diego): tradeoff note: for <256 tokens quantized int8 variants preserve quality for classification and short generation; for long-chained agents we may suggest fp16 or blending. i'll put sample A/B numbers.
13:20 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll include example unit economics per 1M tokens for each model variant so reps can quickly show TCO.
13:45 Speaker 4 (Liam): can you also show expected latency percentile numbers? 95th/99th — that's what customers ask.
14:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes, appendix will include p95/p99 numbers for suggested instance types and caching strategy.
14:28 Speaker 2 (Samantha): question about handoff: who owns the initial scoping call with the customer's infra team? we prefer Redwood SE to do that.
14:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): agreed Redwood SE will do initial technical scoping. Diego will be point for the first two technical calls.
15:02 Speaker 5 (Rina): keep me on the thread for scoping — security will want to be present for peering discussions.
15:15 Speaker 3 (Diego): noted. please send a calendar invite when you have availability.
15:28 Speaker 2 (Samantha): competitive angle — we've lost some deals because procurement wanted everything in their existing cloud marketplace (AWS). can we support an offer that goes via marketplace?
15:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): we have a marketplace pathway for some clouds; it's not uniform. we'll include a procurement options appendix and a recommended objection playbook for reps.
16:05 Speaker 4 (Liam): excellent.
16:18 Speaker 2 (Samantha): also curious if Redwood has an enablement pack for partner reps — decks, playbooks, sample discovery scripts?
16:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes enablement pack will be shared: battlecards, one-pager, sample email templates. we'll attach to the shared folder.
16:48 Speaker 3 (Diego): technical risk — what if customer has strict on-prem only policy? Redwood Private can be packaged but lead times and procurement differ. i'll outline the minimal timeline and cost delta.
17:12 Speaker 2 (Samantha): note for field: on-prem conversations take longer; we'll qualify those early and only engage for strategic deals.
17:30 Speaker 4 (Liam): ok makes sense.
17:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): let's run through a quick sample for Northbridge as a use-case — Liam, can you summarize their ask?
18:00 Speaker 4 (Liam): they want a 2-week pilot to show latency improvements over their current provider, with embed search and chat. immediate win to show improved query relevance plus SLA for p95.
18:25 Speaker 3 (Diego): recommended pilot: dedicated pool, int8 for embeddings, fp16 for chat; KV caching for session agents, p95 target 180-250ms depending on prompt. will draft specifics.
18:48 Speaker 2 (Samantha): sounds good. who will own outreach to the Northbridge CISO? we need exec intro.
19:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Maya to arrange exec sponsor intro (Redwood Head of GTM) with HelioScale VP of Sales.
19:15 Speaker 5 (Rina): i'll prepare our security checklist for them prior to the intro.
19:28 Speaker 2 (Samantha): perfect.
19:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): on approvals — we should define acceptance criteria for pilot success: qualitative feedback on relevance, quantitative on latency and cost per call, and a short buyer-facing report at end of pilot.
20:05 Speaker 3 (Diego): agreed. sample metrics: p95 < 300ms, embed similarity lift +7-10% measured by MAP@10, cost per 1k queries under $X (we'll compute).
20:28 Speaker 4 (Liam): buyers will love the MAP number. please make sure methodology is simple to verify.
20:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, we'll include simple evaluation rubric.
21:00 Speaker 2 (Samantha): for joint outreach, what's the cadence? weekly sync?
21:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): suggest weekly for first month, then biweekly. we'll track pipeline in shared spreadsheet.
21:28 Speaker 5 (Rina): security checkpoints should be on an every-other-week cadence until peering is done.
21:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): noted.
22:00 Speaker 2 (Samantha): any blockers we haven't surfaced?
22:12 Speaker 4 (Liam): procurement timelines could be 8-12 weeks for some accounts. need to manage expectations.
22:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll include procurement playbook and a 1-pager on contracting options.
22:40 Speaker 2 (Samantha): one more ask — can we co-brand some of the demo collateral? helps credibility.
22:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes co-branding ok, we'll share templates.
23:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): small note — for the pilot, we may surface model regressions; we'll add a rollback and fallback policy section to the appendix so HelioScale reps can reassure customers.
23:35 Speaker 2 (Samantha): good idea.
23:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): any final items?
24:00 Speaker 2 (Samantha): no, thanks all.
24:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap: Maya to send deck and pricing; Diego to send perf appendix; Rina to send security questionnaire answers; Samantha to share top-10 accounts list. Exec intro targeted week of 10/26.
24:35 Speaker 4 (Liam): thanks everyone.
24:40 Speaker 5 (Rina): thanks.
24:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): end call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had a few misheard acronyms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cash), some speaker labels generic; cleaned minimally to retain authentic feel.
